title: What the Regulars Order
logline: At a roadside food stall at dusk, a regular orders without looking up, and a friend talks a first-timer into trying the hottest thing on the griddle.
human_question: How much of what we crave is the food, and how much is the ritual of ordering it?

situation.what_happens: A food stall opens for the evening and works until the trade dies. Regulars order the same thing every night without discussion, some of them barely speaking. A group arrives with somebody who has never eaten there, and the others push them into trying the strongest thing on offer. The vendor cooks through all of it at one unvarying pace, and closes up when it is over.
situation.who_is_involved: A vendor and whoever helps them, working a long standing shift; regulars for whom this is part of the day rather than an event; a first-timer and the friends enjoying their reaction.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the vendor, a night's takings and a trade that depends on regulars who will come in any weather. For the regulars, very little, which is exactly what makes it interesting. For the first-timer, a small social test.
situation.how_it_unfolds: An evening's trade rises, peaks and falls, and the same shape repeats nightly until something interrupts it: weather, illness, a licence, a road. Whether the first-timer enjoys it, and whether the regulars say anything at all about why they come, is not arrangeable.

concept_merge.why_together: C004 contributes the everyday sense-sphere world itself, where sight, smell, sound and taste arrive together and are reached for, with delight in one person and flat habit in another. C005 contributes the reminder that ordinary appetite is one of the many occasions on which greed-rooted minds are said to arise, and that eating to quiet hunger is not counted as unwholesome, so nobody at the stall is being accused of anything.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That habit is the quietest form of reaching, and that urging a friend into something is the same reaching arriving by another route. The everyday register makes both visible without any occasion to dress them up.

concept_links.why: This is the digest's own story seed: an evening roadside stall with regulars and first-timers, where sight, smell, sound and taste make up the ordinary sense-sphere world [C004-P:L25] and wanting shows up with joy in some and flat habit in others [C004-M:L17].

Tasty food is among the source's everyday occasions of greed-rooted minds, while eating to relieve hunger is explicitly not counted as unwholesome [C005-M:L5] [C005-M:L13]; the digest warns against turning ordinary appetite into a moral specimen.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Most wanting is not an event. It is an order placed without looking up, and it can also arrive because a friend pushed you into it, and both are the same reaching.
what_must_be_real: The vendor's actual trade and the customers' own words about why they come. No dialogue written for anyone and nobody urged to order for the film.
position_hint: middle, if ever revived: it belongs beside the group's beats on habitual and prompted wanting rather than on its own.
risks: Turning ordinary appetite into a moral specimen
Food-tourism framing that flattens the vendor's working life
Filming on a busy public road
drop_if: No vendor will let a full evening's trade be part of the film

connections.note: Its substance now sits inside IDEA-0021: appetite in its plain everyday form, ordered without a word and eaten without ceremony.

selection.reason: It repeats the prompted-and-unprompted eating beat that IDEA-0021 already carries on the sources' own example; its everyday, unceremonious register is folded into that idea instead.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
